sources.title: NGSS MS-LS1-6: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence for the role of photosynthesis in the cycling of matter and flow of energy into and out of organisms
OpenStax Biology 2e, 30.2 Stems (stomata take in carbon dioxide)
OpenStax Biology 2e, 30.4 Leaves (chloroplasts in the mesophyll)

legend.name: Leaf
legend.meaning: Green from chlorophyll, which captures light

note.text: Almost all the energy in living things started as sunlight.

steps.title: Light
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of sunlight reaching the leaf.

note.text: Light is the energy input for photosynthesis.
Leaf cells are packed with chloroplasts. Their green chlorophyll captures light energy.

steps.title: Vein
steps.instruction: Draw the main vein down the middle.

note.text: Veins carry water into the leaf and carry sugar out to the rest of the plant.
The stalk joins the leaf to the plant.

steps.title: Water in
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of water coming up from the roots.

note.text: Roots take in water, which travels up the stem to the leaf.

steps.title: Carbon dioxide in
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of carbon dioxide going into the leaf.

note.text: Carbon dioxide from the air enters through tiny openings under the leaf, called stomata.

steps.title: Oxygen out
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of oxygen leaving the leaf.

note.text: Oxygen is given off as a waste product. It leaves through the stomata too.

steps.title: Sugar out
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow of sugar going to the rest of the plant.

note.text: The sugar stores the light's energy. The plant uses it to live and to build new leaves, stems and roots.
note.remember: Light energy is stored in sugar.

steps.title: Inputs and outputs
steps.instruction: Pick what each numbered arrow carries.

mistakes.Oxygen: Oxygen leaves the leaf. Carbon dioxide is what goes in.

steps.title: Matter
steps.question: Where does the carbon in the leaf's sugar come from?

options.feedback: Yes. Plants build sugar from carbon dioxide and water, so matter from the air becomes part of the plant.
Roots take in water and minerals. The carbon comes from carbon dioxide in the air.
Light gives energy, not matter. The carbon comes from carbon dioxide.
Oxygen is given off. The carbon comes in as carbon dioxide.

steps.title: Energy
steps.question: A rabbit eats this leaf. Where did the energy in the rabbit's meal first come from?

options.text: The sun: the plant stored light energy in sugar
options.feedback: Right. Photosynthesis brings energy into living things, and it passes along when animals eat plants.
Soil gives minerals and holds water. The energy came from sunlight.
Water is an input, but the energy came from light, stored in sugar.
Animals can't make food from light. The energy came from the sun through the plant.
